written.myAnswer: NH₃ and CN⁻ are Brønsted–Lowry bases that are not Arrhenius bases.
HSO₄⁻ is a Brønsted–Lowry acid because it can donate a proton (H⁺).
Water can act as both an acid and a base: it can donate or accept a proton. Therefore, water is amphoteric.
In water, CO₃²⁻ accepts a proton from H₂O, forming HCO₃⁻ and OH⁻: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻. The OH⁻ formed makes the solution basic.

According to the Arrhenius concept, an acid produces H⁺ in water and a base produces OH⁻ in water. In the Brønsted–Lowry concept, an acid donates a proton and a base accepts a proton; this concept is not restricted to aqueous solutions.
An acid donates a proton. Its conjugate base is the species remaining after that proton is donated and can accept a proton in the reverse reaction.
